---
title: LEF Tools
---

`lef-tools` parses cell LEF (Library Exchange Format) libraries into typed
macros, pins, ports and rectangles through a Rust backend. All geometry stays
in LEF microns; a DEF's `UNITS DISTANCE MICRONS` never changes it. Plain
`.lef` and gzipped `.lef.gz` inputs are both read.

## Install

```bash
cd lef_tools
uv sync --dev
uv run lef-tools --help
```

Or install it from the repository:

```bash
uv tool install "lef-tools @ git+https://github.com/smprather/open-eda-file-tools.git#subdirectory=lef_tools"
```

## Python API

`parse_lef` accepts one path or a sequence of paths. Passing `macros=` streams
every file but materializes only the named `MACRO` bodies; when several files
define the same macro the last definition wins, and every duplicated name is
reported once by `library.duplicate_macro_names()`.

```python
from lef_tools import parse_lef

library = parse_lef(["sky130_fd_sc_hd__buf_8.lef"], macros=["sky130_fd_sc_hd__buf_8"])
macro = library.macro("sky130_fd_sc_hd__buf_8")

print(macro.width_microns, macro.height_microns)
print(macro.origin_x_microns, macro.origin_y_microns)

for pin in macro.pins():
    print(pin.name, pin.direction, pin.use)
    for port in pin.ports():
        print(port.has_unsupported_geometry)
        for rect in port.rects():
            print(rect.layer, rect.x0_microns, rect.y0_microns,
                  rect.x1_microns, rect.y1_microns)
```

`POLYGON`, `PATH` and `VIA` geometry is not exposed yet: a port containing it
sets `has_unsupported_geometry` without dropping the `RECT`s alongside it.
Rectangle coordinates are normalized so `x0 <= x1` and `y0 <= y1`, but negative
and out-of-macro-boundary values are preserved — standard-cell power rails
routinely extend past the macro boundary.

Malformed LEF raises `ValueError` naming the file, macro and pin; unreadable
files raise an `OSError` subclass. Unknown names passed to `library.macro()` or
`macro.pin()` raise `KeyError`.

## Commands

`lef-tools macros` lists every loaded macro with its dimensions as TSV:

```bash
uv run lef-tools macros --lef sky130_fd_sc_hd.lef --lef extra.lef
uv run lef-tools macros --lef sky130_fd_sc_hd.lef --macro sky130_fd_sc_hd__buf_8
```

Columns: `macro, width_um, height_um, origin_x_um, origin_y_um`.

`lef-tools show` prints one macro's dimensions and its pin/port/rect tree:

```bash
uv run lef-tools show --lef sky130_fd_sc_hd.lef --macro sky130_fd_sc_hd__buf_8
```
